Package com.acxiom.emailaudit.utilities

Class HashUtil

java.lang.Object
com.acxiom.emailaudit.utilities.HashUtil
public final class HashUtil extends Object
Stateless utility class providing SHA-256 hashing for files and strings.

Thread safety

All methods are static and stateless. MessageDigest instances are obtained per-call because MessageDigest is not thread-safe; obtaining a fresh instance is cheap and avoids synchronisation entirely.

Design notes

  • File hashing uses a streaming DigestInputStream with a fixed 8 KiB buffer, so arbitrarily large files are handled without loading them fully into heap.
  • HexFormat (Java 17 built-in) produces lowercase hex output without any third-party dependency.
  • NoSuchAlgorithmException is wrapped in an IllegalStateException – SHA-256 is mandated by the JDK spec (JCA, §3.2) and must always be available.

  • Method Details

    • hashFile

      public static String hashFile(Path filePath)
      Computes the SHA-256 hex digest of a file's contents using streaming I/O.
      Parameters:
      filePath - path to the file; must not be null
      Returns:
      lowercase 64-character hex string
      Throws:
      HashUtil.HashComputationException - if the file cannot be read

    • hashFileSafe

      public static String hashFileSafe(Path filePath)
      Computes the SHA-256 hex digest of a file's contents, returning a sentinel value instead of throwing when the file is unreadable.

      The sentinel () is designed to be recognisable in logs but will never match a real hash, so unreadable files are always re-scheduled for processing.

      Parameters:
      filePath - path to the file
      Returns:
      64-character hex string or the sentinel value
